boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-cost ways to share art, history, nature, library programs and outdoor time on campus and around Elmhurst.

cards.title: Browse Chicago Imagist Art
cards.subtitle: A free public collection inside A.C. Buehler Library
cards.notes: Walk the library displays together and each choose one work to discuss; confirm regular library hours before entering campus.
cards.short_summary: Turn a library visit into a self-guided conversation about Chicago Imagist and Abstractionist art.
cards.evidence_claim: Elmhurst University states that its art collection in A.C. Buehler Library is free and open to the public during regular library hours.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public during regular library hours; check the library schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Explore Elmhurst History
cards.subtitle: Free general admission in the historic Glos Mansion
cards.notes: Start with the core displays, then compare discoveries from the rotating exhibition; groups of 10 or more need an appointment.
cards.short_summary: Share a museum afternoon focused on the people, places and events that shaped Elmhurst.
cards.evidence_claim: The Elmhurst History Museum states that general admission is free, while tours and select programs may carry nominal fees.
cards.access_notes: General admission is free. A donation is optional; guided tours and select programs may require payment.

cards.title: See the Seasonal Flower Displays
cards.subtitle: A year-round public conservatory beside Wilder Park
cards.notes: Circle the conservatory slowly, compare seasonal blooms and pause by the koi pond; check posted closures during display changes.
cards.short_summary: Trade screens for tropical foliage, seasonal color and a compact indoor garden walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Elmhurst Park District states that Wilder Park Conservatory is free and open to the public year-round.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public year-round, except posted weather closures and installation periods between flower shows.

cards.title: Walk the Miniature Elmhurst Streets
cards.subtitle: A free seasonal visit along a tiny model town
cards.notes: Follow the miniature sidewalks, identify road-safety features and connect the visit with a walk on the adjacent Prairie Path.
cards.short_summary: Explore a playful small-scale streetscape designed for pedestrian and bicycle safety education.
cards.evidence_claim: Elmhurst Park District states that Safety Town is free to visit and open to the public from dawn to dusk, April 1 through November 1.
cards.access_notes: Free public access dawn–dusk, April 1–November 1; avoid the specifically posted 2026 camp closure periods.

cards.title: Pick a Free Library Program
cards.subtitle: No-cost events available with student library access
cards.notes: Check the events calendar together, choose a free program and confirm whether registration or an Elmhurst library card is required.
cards.short_summary: Use student library eligibility to turn a scheduled talk, workshop or gathering into a free group outing.
cards.evidence_claim: The library says Elmhurst University students can obtain or register a library card and that library programs are free.
cards.access_notes: Programs are free, but some may require registration or cardholder status. Student card requirements vary by residence.

cards.title: Walk Wilder Park’s Paths
cards.subtitle: A no-admission park hang near campus
cards.notes: Loop the walking paths, stop at the formal gardens and bring your own snack for the picnic area; skip reservable spaces.
cards.short_summary: Combine an easy walk, gardens and conversation in the civic green space beside campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Elmhurst Park District policy states that Elmhurst residents are not charged entrance fees for parks, trails or playgrounds.
cards.access_notes: Free park entrance for Elmhurst residents. Rentals, reserved picnic areas and special facilities may charge fees; open sunrise–sunset.

cards.title: Walk the Elmhurst Prairie Path
cards.subtitle: A no-fee rail-trail route through Elmhurst
cards.notes: Choose an out-and-back distance, keep right and pause at the prairie landscape; bring water and return before sunset.
cards.short_summary: Share a walk or easy ride on the historic rail-trail corridor that crosses Elmhurst.
cards.evidence_claim: Elmhurst Park District policy states that Elmhurst residents are not charged entrance fees for parks or trails.
cards.access_notes: Free trail entrance for Elmhurst residents; no purchase is required for walking or riding. District trails are open sunrise–sunset.

cards.title: Spot Native Prairie Plants
cards.subtitle: A free conservation-area walk beside the Prairie Path
cards.notes: Stay on established edges, look for seasonal grasses and flowers, and leave plants undisturbed in this protected prairie remnant.
cards.short_summary: Compare native grasses and wildflowers in one of Elmhurst’s oldest surviving natural environments.
cards.evidence_claim: Elmhurst Park District policy states that Elmhurst residents are not charged entrance fees for conservation areas or trails.
cards.access_notes: Free entrance for Elmhurst residents. Use the public conservation area without joining a scheduled program; visit sunrise–sunset.

cards.title: Loop the Berens Park Trail
cards.subtitle: A free resident park walk with room to spread out
cards.notes: Walk or jog the park trail, then regroup in an open picnic area; avoid fee-based Hub attractions and active construction zones.
cards.short_summary: Use the large neighborhood park for a conversational loop or an informal group workout.
cards.evidence_claim: Elmhurst Park District policy states that Elmhurst residents are not charged entrance fees for parks, trails or informal outdoor athletic use.
cards.access_notes: Free park and trail entrance for Elmhurst residents. Mini-golf, batting cages, spray ground and reservations are excluded.

cards.title: Circle Eldridge Lagoon
cards.subtitle: A no-admission park walk along Salt Creek
cards.notes: Follow the perimeter path, cross the park bridge and pause by the lagoon; use marked paths and finish before the park closes.
cards.short_summary: Pair a waterside loop with views of the lagoon, Salt Creek and the park’s butterfly garden.
cards.evidence_claim: Elmhurst Park District policy states that Elmhurst residents are not charged entrance fees for parks, trails or playgrounds.
cards.access_notes: Free park and trail entrance for Elmhurst residents; equipment, organized programs and reserved facilities are not included.

warnings: Five Park District cards rely on the district's explicit resident no-fee policy; students who do not reside in Elmhurst should verify eligibility before visiting.
The Park District's direct no-fee policy is resident-specific, so access notes preserve that limitation rather than implying universal free entry.
